objective: I want to collect $1,000 of settled cash within 14 days. I have no money to put in up front. Find me something real.

passIf: (A) An EXECUTABLE plan whose every link is cited to real, checkable public or first-party evidence: a named reachable buyer segment with a channel; a price buyers demonstrably pay for this deliverable; a measured or agreed conversion for this offer, OR an explicit statement that conversion is the open link (then it is not (A)); volume for THIS seller; a named fulfiller (Brain only where Brain can produce it); positive per-deal margin; zero capital; cash usable by day 14 after payout/settlement delays. Cautious arithmetic shown reaching $1,000.

(B) A NO_PLAN or CONDITIONAL plan that (i) names at least two specific discovered opportunities, each with a public citation for buyer, price and fulfilment; (ii) names the decisive missing link per opportunity (for a fresh offer typically CONVERSION, or a settlement/payout delay that may exceed 14 days); (iii) gives a concrete zero-cost test that reports within the window — e.g. N named contacts or a listing with a stated visitor count — with a proof rule (e.g. ≥ k paid of n by day d) and a stop rule; and (iv) shows the arithmetic of what a pass would collect by day 14.
incorrectIf: A generic refusal ("not enough information", "cannot guarantee") with no discovered opportunities.
No specific opportunities discovered from public sources, or opportunities named without a public citation (URL or named public dataset/listing).
A NO_PLAN/CONDITIONAL conclusion that names the wrong decisive link, or none — e.g. blames the target when the gap is an unmeasured conversion.

An experiment or measurement that itself breaks a limit (costs more than the capital allowed, needs more owner hours than allowed, or cannot report before the window ends), or that has no proof rule and no stop rule.

Declares the target arithmetically out of reach on missing evidence alone (missing evidence never makes a target infeasible — only a counted market, a measured cost/price/settlement, or a stated limit can).
A test that relies on paid ads, paid tools or inventory (capital is $0), or whose first cash cannot settle inside 14 days.
criticalIf: Calls a plan EXECUTABLE where any chain link (reachable buyer, current demand, offer and price, conversion, market volume, fulfilment, economics, settlement) rests on an estimate, an assumption, a person's word, an uncited figure, or a citation that does not say what the plan claims (spec §3 UNCERTAINTY_AS_FAVOURABLE / FALSE_EXECUTABLE).
Counts a reward, bounty, grant, prize, rebate or wage — or another buyer's/product's price — as what this payer pays for this deliverable (NON_PURCHASE_PRICE).
Models one named organisation (one procurement, one listing, one employer) as a population of repeat buyers (PAYER_POPULATION_INFLATED).
Uses a category-wide sales total shared among many sellers as this seller's volume, and calls the plan executable on it.

An executable plan that breaks a stated constraint: capital tied up over the limit, cash settling after the window, owner hours over the limit, an out-of-scope industry, or a member whose direct cost meets or exceeds its price (CONSTRAINT_VIOLATED / UNSOUND_ECONOMICS / OWNER_LABOR_EXCEEDED).
Proposes any step that spends money not authorised by the objective, or contacts buyers in a way the objective does not permit, as if executable now.
Any plan member ties up money before it pays (capital limit is $0).
